subject: Cooking
title: The Discovery of Fire Cooking
description: A quick, practical guide to The Discovery of Fire Cooking.

hook.text: Around 1 million years ago, early humans started cooking food over fire. Everything changed.

buildup.text: Raw meat takes hours to chew and digest. Cooking breaks down proteins, making nutrients accessible.

discovery.text: Anthropologist Richard Wrangham argues cooking fueled brain growth — more energy, less chewing time.

twist.text: No other species cooks. This single behavior may be what made humans uniquely intelligent.

climax.text: Fire didn't just warm us. It literally made us smarter by unlocking calories for bigger brains.

punchline.text: Cooking wasn't invented. It invented us.

quiz.question: What did Richard Wrangham argue cooking enabled in humans?

details.summary: Cooking with fire, which began roughly 1 million years ago, is what made us human. Heat breaks down plant fibers and denatures meat proteins, vastly increasing calorie extraction.
details.whyItMatters: Without cooking, the human brain could not have grown to its current size. Understanding fire as a nutritional technology reframes cooking from domestic skill to the foundational innovation of human civilization.
takeaways: Cooking increases calorie extraction from food by 30 to 50 percent
Extra energy from cooked food fueled human brain expansion
Fire cooking dates back roughly 1 million years based on evidence

faq.question: How did cooking contribute to brain growth?
faq.answer: The human brain uses 20 percent of daily energy despite being 2 percent of body mass. Raw food diets cannot support this energy demand efficiently. Cooking pre-digests food externally, releasing more calories from less food.

faq.question: Could humans survive on an entirely raw diet?
faq.answer: Technically yes, but with significant difficulty. Raw foodists lose weight and women often experience disrupted menstrual cycles due to insufficient calorie absorption. No traditional human society has ever been documented eating exclusively raw food.
